'''Christina Eubanks-Turner''' is a professor of mathematics in the Seaver College of Science and Engineering at [[Loyola Marymount University]] (LMU). Her academic areas of interest include graph theory, commutative algebra, [[mathematics education]], and mathematical sciences diversification. She is also the Director of the Master's Program in Teaching Mathematics at LMU.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2019-12-04|title=Faculty Enhances Teachers' Knowledge in Master's Program|url=https://seavernews.lmu.edu/2019/12/04/faculty-enhances-teachers-knowledge-in-masters-program/|access-date=2020-06-10|website=Seaver News|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Eubanks-Turner was born and raised in [[New Orleans|New Orleans, Louisiana]] and enjoyed logic puzzles and creative thinking as a child.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Christina Eubanks Turner|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/christina_eubanks_turner/|access-date=2020-06-10|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Episode 21: Christina Eubanks-Turner|url=https://www.sheheroes.org/videos/episode-21-christina-eubanks/|access-date=2020-06-10|website=SheHeroes|language=en-US}}</ref> She received her B.S. ''cum laude'' from [[Xavier University of Louisiana]], a [[Historically black colleges and universities|historically black college]], in 2002; she received her M.S. in 2004 and her Ph.D. in 2008—both from the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]].<ref name=":1" />  Eubanks-Turner was one of the first two African Americans to receive a doctorate degree in mathematics from the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.<ref name=":3">{{Cite book|last=Jones|first=Shelly|title=Women Who Count: Honoring African American Women Mathematicians|publisher=American Mathematical Society|year=2019|isbn=9781470448899}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |editor=Henrich, Allison K. |editor2=Lawrence, Emille D. |editor3=Pons, Matthew A. |editor4=Taylor, David George |title=Living proof : stories of resilience along the mathematical journey|year=2019|publisher=American Mathematical Society |isbn=978-1-4704-5281-0|oclc=1097363982}}</ref> Her dissertation explored the topic of "Prime ideals in low-dimensional mixed polynomial/[[power series]] rings."<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Eubanks-Turner|first=Christina|date=2008-01-01|title=Prime ideals in low-dimensional mixed polynomial/power series rings|url=https://digitalcommons.unl.edu/dissertations/AAI3303652|journal=ETD Collection for University of Nebraska - Lincoln|pages=1–114}}</ref> Eubanks-Turner's [[doctoral advisor]] was [[Sylvia Wiegand]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Christina Eubanks-Turner - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=137424 |access-date=2023-01-04 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
Eubanks-Turner was the first African American to receive tenure at LMU's College of Science and Engineering.<ref name=":3" />

Her research areas include specialized mathematical training that teachers need to teach math at the undergraduate and secondary levels.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Alison Castro Superfine|last2=Wenjuan Li|last3=Mara V. Martinez|date=2013|title=Developing Preservice Teachers' Mathematical Knowledge for Teaching: Making Explicit Design Considerations for a Content Course|journal= Mathematics Teacher Educator|volume=2|issue=1|pages=42–54|doi=10.5951/mathteaceduc.2.1.0042|issn=2167-9789}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Eubanks-Turner|first1=Christina|last2=Beaulieu|first2=Patricia|last3=Pal|first3=Nabendu|s2cid=126066979|date=2018-02-07|title=Smooth Transition for Advancement to Graduate Education (STAGE) for Underrepresented Groups in the Mathematical Sciences Pilot Project: Broadening Participation through Mentoring|journal=PRIMUS|language=en|volume=28|issue=2|pages=97–117|doi=10.1080/10511970.2017.1295409|issn=1051-1970|doi-access=free}}</ref> Her pedagogy also includes the integration of equity issues<ref>{{Cite web|title=Equity In Mathematics Education: Five Mathematicians Reflect On The 2018 PCMI Workshop|url=http://digitaleditions.walsworthprintgroup.com/article/Equity+In+Mathematics+Education%3A+Five+Mathematicians+Reflect+On+The+2018+PCMI+Workshop/3247828/546728/article.html|access-date=2020-06-10|website=digitaleditions.walsworthprintgroup.com|language=en-US}}</ref> into teaching and an approach to mathematics education that addresses the whole student.<ref name=":2" /> Her research in mathematics includes topics in [[graph theory]] and [[commutative algebra]].<ref name=":5">{{Citation|last1=Celikbas|first1=Ela|chapter=Prime Ideals in Polynomial and Power Series Rings over Noetherian Domains|date=2014|title=Commutative Algebra|pages=55–82|editor-last=Fontana|editor-first=Marco|publisher=Springer New York|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-1-4939-0925-4_4|isbn=978-1-4939-0924-7|last2=Eubanks-Turner|first2=Christina|last3=Wiegand|first3=Sylvia|editor2-last=Frisch|editor2-first=Sophie|editor3-last=Glaz|editor3-first=Sarah}}</ref>
